data.title: Core inflation eases to 2% in September as retail costs cool
data.description:
Telecommunication service prices fell by a larger margin.

Core inflation eased to 2% year-on-year (YoY) in September, from 2.2% in August, as services and retail prices eased, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) reported.

On a month-on-month basis, core prices rose by 0.1% in September, whilst the all-items consumer price index (CPI) eased to 2.2% from 2.3% in August.

Services inflation eased to 1.7% YoY from 2% in August due to a smaller increase in point-to-point transport service costs and a larger decline in telecommunication service prices.

Retail and other goods inflation moderated to 1.2% from 1.8% as furniture prices declined and clothing prices rose at a slower pace.

Private transport inflation slipped to 7.1% from 7.5% due to a moderate increase in car prices.

Electricity and gas inflation held at 8.7%, whilst accommodation inflation edged up to 0.9% from 0.8% as housing rents increased at a faster pace.

Food inflation also rose to 2.4% from 2.3% due to higher inflation in both non-cooked food and food services.

MAS projected the core inflation to average 1.5-2.0% in 2026 and 1.5-2.5% in 2027. CPI-all items inflation is forecast at around 2.0% in 2026 and 1.5-2.5% in 2027.

data.title: Industrial prices up 4.2% outpace rents in Q3 as occupancy eases
data.description:
Warehouse was the only segment with rising occupancy at 89.7% in Q3.

Singapore industrial property prices outpaced rents in the third quarter, rising 4.2% year-on-year (YoY) against rental growth of 2.1%, according to JTC.

Overall occupancy eased 0.2 percentage points quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) and year-on-year to 88.9%.

JTC attributed the decrease to tenants vacating older single-user factory and multiple-user factories to be developed and slower demand for suburban business park.

Overall rental index rose by 0.5% QoQ and 2.1% YoY in line with inflation. Overall price index rose at a slightly faster pace of 1.0% QoQ and 4.2% YoY, amidst resilient demand and low interest rates.

Warehouse was the only segment that saw an increase in occupancy, up 0.3 percentage points QoQ to 89.7%, whilst multiple-user factory stood at 90.3%, single-user factory at 89.1%, and business park at 77.2%.

All segments saw an uptick in rent, with Multiple-User Factory up 0.3% QoQ and 1.6% YoY, followed by Single-User Factory up 0.7% QoQ and 3.1% YoY, Business Park up 0.1% QoQ and 0.7% YoY and Warehouse up 1% QoQ and 2.8% YoY.

Prices increased for all segments, with multiple-user factory up 1.1% QoQ and 5.3% YoY, whilst single-user factory rose 0.8% QoQ and 1.5% YoY.

For industrial government land sales in Q3, tenders for two single-user sites and one multiple-user site closed.

6 Tuas Avenue 14, a single-user development, and 5 Tuas Avenue 13, a multiple-user development, were successfully awarded, whilst the single-user site at Jalan Besut closed with no bids crossing the reserve price.

JTC allocated a total of 80,400 sq m of ready-built facilities to industrialists in Q3, with total returns of 105,800 sq m. About 71% of returns were due to natural expiries or consolidation of operations.

JTC forecasts 0.3 mil sq m of supply to be completed in Q4, according to planning approvals as of end-September. 56% of the supply is single-user factory space, whilst 44% is for warehouses.

An average annual supply of 1.2 mil sq m of industrial space is expected to be completed between 2027 to 2030, with about 59% for single-user factory space.

data.title: Keppel DC REIT distribution per unit jumps 11.7% in 9M
data.description:
Distributable income also rose 16.7% to $228m.

Keppel DC REIT recorded a distribution per unit (DPU) of $0.08571 in the first nine months (9M) of 2026, 11.7% higher than $0.07670 a year earlier.

Distributable income rose 16.7% to $228m, from $195.3m in 9M 2025, driven by stronger operating performance, contributions from acquisitions, and increased effective interests in Keppel DC Singapore 3 and 4.

The REIT said the gains were partially offset by higher finance costs from acquisition loans drawn in the fourth quarter of 2025 and the lease extension consideration for Keppel DC Singapore 7 and 8.

Gross revenue also increased 13.3% to $365.3m from $322.4m, whilst net property income (NPI) grew 13.1% to $316.8m from $280.2m.

NPI growth reflected positive rental reversions and escalations and the acquisition of Tokyo Data Centre 3, but was partially offset by the divestment of Kelsterbach Data Centre and the absence of income from Cardiff Data Centre.

Contracted power capacity stood at about 96%, whilst portfolio occupancy edged up to 93%.

The REIT also recorded a portfolio rental reversion of about 14% and secured renewals and new contracts in Singapore and Australia.

data.title: CapitaLand names Hsieh Fu Hua chairman from January 2027
data.description:
Temasek's Png Chin Yee will also join the board.

CapitaLand Investment (CLI) has named Hsieh Fu Hua as board chairman and Png Chin Yee as non-executive non-independent director, effective 1 January 2027.

The appointments come as the group updates its board of directors and advances its next phase of growth, CLI said.

Hsieh will succeed retiring chairman Miguel Ko, whilst Png will replace Gabriel Lim Meng Liang as non-executive non-independent director when their terms end on 31 December.

Png is currently the president of Temasek Singapore, with experience in investment management, finance, capital markets, and corporate transformation, CLI said.

“As CLI enters its next phase, our CEO, Lee Chee Koon, has my full support. I look forward
to working closely with him and the management team to address our strategic priorities
and execute them with discipline,” Hsieh said.

data.title: Trio conservation shophouses in Tanjong Pagar for sale
data.description:
Buyers may submit offers for individual shophouses or the entire portfolio.

A collection of three conservation shophouses along Tanjong Pagar Road is up for sale at a guide price of $43m via an Expression of Interest (EOI) until 26 November, according to sole agent CBRE.

The portfolio consists of 83, 91 and 97 Tanjong Pagar Road properties, with a combined land area of approximately 4,022 square feet (sq ft) and a total floor area of approximately 11,306 sq ft, subject to final survey.

83 and 91 Tanjong Pagar Road are both three-storey shophouses with attics, sitting on a land area of 1,291 sq ft and a floor area of 3,828 sq ft, respectively. Each is sold at $14.5m.

97 Tanjong Pagar Road is a two-storey shophouse with an attic, with a total land area of 1,444 sq ft and a floor area of 3,650 sq ft. It is being sold for $14m.

Buyers can purchase the properties individually or as a whole for a guide price of $43m.

The properties are located within the Tanjong Pagar Conservation Area in District 2, a sought-after food & beverage (F&B) and lifestyle precinct.

The portfolio is within walking distance of major office developments such as Guoco Tower, International Plaza, and Frasers Tower.

The shophouses are currently occupied by a diversified mix of established long-term F&B, retail and office operators.

All three shophouses are zoned commercial, with no Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty or Seller’s Stamp Duty payable.

data.title: TSH responds to SGX haze queries, cites no fires
data.description:
The company said it enforced a zero-burning policy from May 2009.

TSH Resources said no fire was detected within its planted or operational areas from January to 21 October in response to the Singapore Exchange’s (SGX) queries over the transboundary haze.

In a filing with Bursa Malaysia and SGX, the group reported 274 hotspots within its estate boundaries and community enclave areas, all of which were extinguished by field teams, with police reports lodged.

It claimed it had received no reports or claims of fires started by its employees during the period.

The group also maintained that its operations in Indonesia had not contributed to the haze.

TSH reported a localised fire in August within an area belonging to its subsidiary Bulungan Citra Agro Persada, which was extinguished on the same day.

Separately, Apical Group’s sustainability department had queried hotspots at another subsidiary, Farinda Bersaudara, which TSH said occurred in a community enclave outside its operational area.

The group said it had received no other formal inquiries or notices from environmental authorities regarding the haze.

TSH has enforced a zero-burning policy since May 2009 and has not developed new plantings on peat since December 2015, it noted.

Its fire prevention measures include a satellite-based monitoring platform that detects hotspots and land clearing, 28 firefighting squads comprising 425 trained personnel, and daily ground patrols in three shifts.

The group said it also operates 123 fire towers and 11 drones, monitors hotspots within a 2-km buffer beyond its concession boundaries.

It cited cooperation with local communities, government agencies, and neighbouring companies on fire prevention and response.

data.title: Malaysian and Thai central banks join SG’s BLOOM
data.description:
They will ensure policy and regulatory considerations are taken into account.

Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Bank of Thailand (BOT) have joined the Borderless, Liquid, Open, Online, Multi-currency (BLOOM) initiative as policymaker members, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced on 23 October.

BLOOM is a public-private initiative that brings together policymakers, financial institutions, payment networks, and technology providers to advance the use of digital money in cross-border financial activity.

Through BLOOM, the central banks will partner with industry players in their respective jurisdictions to develop common approaches to how digital money, including tokenised deposits and regulated stablecoins, can be accepted, exchanged, and settled across institutions, networks, and jurisdictions.

MAS said the participation of central banks will ensure that public policy and regulatory considerations are taken into account as these approaches are developed.

"The future of finance will involve multiple forms of digital money operating across different institutions and markets,” said Leong Sing Chiong, deputy managing director for markets and development at MAS.

“To fully harness the benefits of using digital money, collaboration among policymakers and industry participants will be needed to address practical issues around acceptance, settlement and interoperability,” he added.

BNM and BOT join 26 other BLOOM participants, including industry members Airwallex, Mastercard, Maybank, Monee, Nium, Ripple, ShopeePay, and Visa.

The World Bank Group has also joined, contributing its experience in payment systems modernisation, cross-border payments, and financial inclusion.

data.title: NTUC-KPMG programme to redesign jobs around AI
data.description:
Firms can tap an NTUC grant to aid workplace transformation.

The National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and KPMG Singapore have launched a transformation programme to help firms translate artificial intelligence (AI) adoption into business gains and better jobs.

The two groups have inked a partnership to collaborate on supporting companies in areas such as workforce planning, job redesign, worker training, and technology adoption as AI reshapes jobs.

The Labour Movement wants workers to be able to adapt to AI-driven changes and benefit from the opportunities they create, said Chee Meng, NTUC secretary-general.

The programme allows companies to tap the NTUC Company Training Committee Grant and Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package at different stages of their workplace transformation, from planning to implementation.

Companies will then be supported in planning their future manpower needs and redesigning jobs around higher-value work, whilst reskilling or redeploying employees into new or expanded roles.

NTUC LearningHub and KPMG have also agreed to collaborate on six capability-building courses spanning AI transformation, AI in sustainability, and AI in finance.

The two organisations said they aim for better jobs, wages, and work prospects for workers alongside improvements in business productivity.

data.title: Suntec REIT distribution per unit climbs 13% in Q3
data.description:
Distributable income stood at $59.9m, up 14.3% YoY.

Suntec REIT lists a strong third quarter (Q3), with distribution per unit (DPU) at $0.02017, 13.4% higher than $0.01710 last year.

Distributable income increased by 14.3% year on year (YoY) to $59.9m from $52.4m, payable by 27 November.

Gross revenue is up by 5.2% to $123.6m. Net property income records 6.2% growth to 83.4m YoY, attributable to strong portfolio performance in both office and retail markets.

Suntec’s YoY committed occupancy for office space rose to 99.6% from 98.5%, whilst retail is down to 98.6% from 99.3%.

Rent reversion grew on both portfolios, with office and retail up by 7.3% and 11.2%, respectively.

Retention rates for office and retail are 87% and 83%, respectively.  

“We remain focused on optimising our portfolio, strengthening our balance sheet and enhancing long-term returns for our unitholders,” said Chong Kee Hiong, CEO of Suntec.

data.title: HDB resale prices fall for third straight quarter as sales rebound
data.description:
Approved rental applications fell 6.2% to 9,381 in Q3.

HDB resale price index edged down 0.1% quarter on quarter to 202.5 in the third quarter (Q3), marking its third consecutive quarterly decline, whilst resale transactions rose 19.5% to 7,645.

A 23 October statement from HDB said the decrease followed declines of 0.1% in the first quarter and 0.3% in the second quarter (Q2).

Resale transactions rose 5.9% year on year from 7,221 in Q3 2025.

Approved applications to rent out HDB flats slipped by 6.2% to 9,381 from 10,002 in Q2.

As at the end of Q3, 59,378 HDB flats were rented out, edging up 0.9% from 58,855 in the previous quarter.

HDB said it had observed no significant increase in resale prices or purchases by private residential property owners and former owners since the 15-month wait-out period was removed on 28 July 2026.

It will launch about 7,960 flats in Bedok, Geylang, Sembawang, Tengah, Toa Payoh, and Yishun in November, including Community Care Apartments in Toa Payoh.

“The macroeconomic outlook remains highly uncertain, including for global and domestic interest rates,” HDB said. “Households are advised to exercise prudence when purchasing property and taking out mortgage loans.”
